We have a double garage but only use one door - if you are the same, this is a great idea for the unused door.

For this, it helps if you are on the artistic side. If you aren't you could do something similar but use tombstones instead, (i'd cut out the RIP on them so the light shines through) it will still give an impact but just a simple, easier design.

What you would need:

  • Outdoor lights (make sure they are for outdoor use, we don't want anyone getting zapped, killed and becoming part of their creepy yard display)
  • Foam sheeting - you can get this in various sizes and price points. I prefer the stuff with the foil coating as you can paint by hand or spray paint it without fear of the chemicals in the paint eating away at it.
  • Outdoor paint or spray paint - I get my spray paint at the dollar stores or Lowes - the cheapest one is fine as long as it is matte, you don't want it shiny!
  • Box cutter, Xacto knife or a hot foam cutter (available at craft stores, use a coupon!) - I like using a hot foam cutter as it gives much cleaner lines and doesn't leave it looking jagged.
  • Whatever design you come up with, let your imagination run wild - just make sure that whatever idea you have, it all stays connected at the bottom to give you room to hide the lights behind it.
  • OPTIONAL - get a cheap long piece of wood to attach your foam board designs to (if you are using several sheets), this will help it to stop blowing away in the wind also.

How to:

  • Paint your foam boards black
  • Trace out your design on them
  • Cut out your design
  • Attach wood to the bottom of your design
  • Run the lighting at the bottom of your garage door - color of lights is totally up to you. Green, red, purple and orange are great choices
  • Place your cut out in front of the lights so the bottom of the cut outs hides the lighting behind it.

Now stand back and check out how it looks!
